issue.title: Finish usage-limit auto-disable correctness and surfaces
issue.description: Usage-limit failures atomically establish one provider-disable window across concurrent agents, retry decisions stay attributed to the provider that actually failed after overrides and fallbacks, user pattern replacement is literal, and the promised provenance, configuration, documentation, and end-to-end acceptance coverage are present.

issue.title: Make first usage-limit disable atomic in sase-core
issue.description: atomic-disable: add a Rust-core and Python-binding operation that atomically writes a provider disable only when no active record exists, returns whether this caller won the window, preserves the existing unconditional manual replacement APIs, and proves first-writer behavior under real contention.

issue.title: Correct matching, provider attribution, and end-to-end behavior
issue.description: runtime-correctness: consume the atomic store result in usage-limit enforcement, make replace_patterns literal even for an empty list, keep retry attribution pinned to the execution provider recorded for each attempt including fallback attempts, and add a full fakey invocation-to-disable-to-notification acceptance test that proves one attempt, unchanged error propagation, and no collateral provider disable.

issue.title: Restore disable provenance and document usage-limit policy
issue.description: surface-and-document: render automatic, manual, and unknown disable provenance in the current split Launch Control provider modules and top-bar tooltip, add the commented usage_limit configuration block without disturbing newer config fields, document detection, reset hints, machine-wide expiry, clearing, retry precedence, and extension/replacement semantics, and cover the surfaces including intentional visual snapshots.

DISCOVERED ISSUE: tests/test_provider_disable.py::test_facade_try_disable_one_winner_under_process_contention fails intermittently under the full parallel lane. Seen 2026-08-19 in workspace sase_12 at HEAD bdc3f2f74 during an unrelated statistics_pane.py module split: 'just check' escalated to the full 14-worker lane (3 failed, 33880 passed in 361s) and this node failed on gw5; the exact node then passed serially with -p no:randomly in 0.74s on the same tree.

MECHANISM: the test spawns 6 worker processes that all call try_disable_provider('claude', ...) at once. One worker exited 1 with 'RuntimeError: timed out waiting for the provider-disable state lock' raised from src/sase/llm_provider/provider_disable.py:193 (the PyO3 try-set binding), so the assert process.returncode == 0 at tests/test_provider_disable.py:176 failed. The lock-acquire timeout inside the Rust provider-disable state store is sized for 6 contending processes on an idle box; under a 14-worker xdist lane those 6 subprocesses are competing with ~14 other pytest workers, so a loser can starve past the timeout. Same shape as ready flake task sase-qp (a fixed stale window that cannot survive holder starvation).

WHY THIS EPIC: try_disable_provider and this contention test both came from commit 665a22ac5 ('feat(llm-provider): add atomic first-writer disable facade'), whose message whitelists the facade symbols as 'unused-until-n4.5.2' — this epic's own first-writer work owns the lock and its timeout, so the fix (raise/derive the acquire timeout, or make the test tolerate a starved loser) belongs here rather than in a standalone flake task.

NOT REPRODUCED SINCE: one occurrence; I did not run a contention lane to re-measure.

CORROBORATION of the 2026-08-19T03:32:27Z DISCOVERED ISSUE above (test_facade_try_disable_one_winner_under_process_contention): that note recorded 'NOT REPRODUCED SINCE: one occurrence'. It is not one occurrence. The selection-health record store holds a second, independent failure of the same node from a different workspace and head two days earlier: 20260817T225808Z-24f0c9539656-1625482-full-run.json (workspace sase_18, HEAD 24f0c9539656, mode fast, exit 1), whose changed_files are entirely glossary/completion CLI files with no relation to provider_disable. The known 20260819T032227Z record (workspace sase_12, HEAD bdc3f2f74c51) is the second. Two workspaces, two heads, 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-19, both with unrelated dirty trees.

CONSEQUENCE: the node now trips the flake baseline gate. 'just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake' fails with 'flake baseline gate: 1 reproducible flake(s) exceed tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt', naming only this node, so it blocks every agent's landing rather than just this epic's. I confirmed it is not a live regression: it passes 3/3 serially at 0e36971e0 under '.venv/bin/python -m pytest <node> -q -p no:randomly' (2.6s each).

ACTION TAKEN: the sase-qn land agent added this node to tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt attributed to this bead, following the file's stated convention that an addition names the owning bead. That unblocks landing; it does not discharge the debt. The fix the note above proposes (raise or derive the Rust provider-disable lock-acquire timeout, or make the test tolerate a starved loser) still belongs to this epic, and landing it should replace the baseline entry with a '# fixed-at:' line rather than a bare deletion. No separate flake task was filed, per /sase_new_task's active-epic branch.

DISCOVERED ISSUE: tests/test_llm_provider_usage_limit_disable.py::TestHandlePossibleUsageLimit::test_codex_reset_at_date_failure_writes_until_disable_at_parsed_instant fails deterministically as of 2026-08-20.

REPRO: isolated rerun on workspace sase_17 at HEAD 6d87cf227 after just install: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_llm_provider_usage_limit_disable.py::TestHandlePossibleUsageLimit::test_codex_reset_at_date_failure_writes_until_disable_at_parsed_instant -q` -> 1 failed. Same node failed in an escalated just check full-suite lane (1 failed / 34963 passed / 13 skipped). Rerun on the same tree also failed, so this is not a flake.

FAILURE: `assert result is not None` at tests/test_llm_provider_usage_limit_disable.py:146. Captured log: `ValueError: expires_at must be in the future` from src/sase/llm_provider/provider_disable.py:257 (`try_disable_provider_until` -> Rust binding). handle_possible_usage_limit swallows that and returns None.

ROOT CAUSE: the fixture's verbatim Codex text (`_CODEX_TRY_AGAIN_AT_DATE`) names an absolute reset of `Aug 20th, 2026 6:38 AM`. The test freezes `sase.llm_provider.usage_limit_config.time.time` at 2026-08-17 06:38 UTC so the parser still treats that instant as future, but `try_disable_provider_until` validates `expires_at` against wall-clock now (the monkeypatch does not reach the binding). On 2026-08-20 after 06:39 UTC that parsed instant is in the past, so the disable is rejected. Expected expires_at in the test is `datetime(2026, 8, 20, 6, 38, tzinfo=UTC).timestamp() + 60`.

WHY THIS EPIC: this node and the until-disable path it exercises landed with the usage-limit auto-disable work; the remaining n4.5.4 phases (published first-writer core release, Antigravity xsmall-only routing) do not obviously include it, but the parser, `try_disable_provider_until`, and this fixture are this epic's.

NOT CAUSED BY THE DISCOVERING DIFF: alias-history Ctrl+J/K 10-run step (src/sase/ace/tui/modals/alias_history_{state,modal}.py plus their tests and docs). No usage-limit files were touched.

LIKELY FIX: freeze the same now into the disable binding (or pass `now=` through `try_disable_provider_until`), or replace the hardcoded Aug 20 2026 calendar date with an instant computed from the frozen now.
